content:
Priya: ran an overnight sweep against qwen-32b with our heterogeneous quant profiles (fp8/int8/4bit). noticed a consistent tail-latency regression when the kernel selector prefers fp8 attention kernels on long-context runs (seq=4096). attaching quick perf dump below.

Priya: ```
model: qwen-32b
profile: hetero_fp8_int8.json
batch: 4 seq: 4096
kernel_choice: fp8_attn_v2 (selected)
throughput: 420 tok/s
p50: 8ms p95: 42ms p99: 182ms
when forcing int8_attn: throughput: 460 tok/s p99: 156ms
notes: kv_hit_rate ~0.77, cache_evictions spike during generation windows
```

Alex: can you paste the exact command you used to collect the kernel stats?

Priya: `./perf/profile_runner --model qwen-32b --quant-profile configs/hetero_fp8_int8.json --seq 4096 --batch 4 --dump-kernel-stats --iterations 300`

Marco: hmm that p99 delta looks big. my guess: fp8_attn_v2 has a slightly different memory access pattern and when kv cache pressure hits it triggers micro-evictions -> host transfers -> tail. seen something similar on a Mistral run last month.

Jun: adding context: fp8 kernels sometimes add extra pre/post cast ops that don't fuse with our KV copy path. on high seq lengths those extra ops push attention into an unfavored codepath. calibration can also insert per-head scaling which makes fuse rules miss.

Sara: quick mitigation: we can force kernel selector rule to prefer int8 for seq >= 2048 or when kv_hit_rate < 0.8. trivial flag: `kernel_selector.override_precision_on_long_context=true`

Pat: can we instead change batching heuristic? for long seq, reduce max_batch to 2 for fp8-enabled nodes so we avoid concurrent KV pressure spikes. cheaper than disabling fp8 entirely.

Priya: verified: forcing int8 removes the p99 regression but reduces throughput ~9% (460 -> 420 tok/s). so tradeoff: latency vs cost.

perf-bot: perf-ci: nightly qwen-32b mixed-quant sweep: baseline (hetero_fp8_int8) vs force-int8: p99 improved by 14% when forcing int8 on seq>=2048. regression flagged: #perf-2026-042.

Alex: proposal: new heuristic in kernel selector: prefer fp8 only when BOTH avg_seq <= 1024 AND kv_hit_rate >= 0.85. else fallback to int8. also record a per-deploy telemetry flag `kernel_choice_reason` for later analysis.

Jun: also add a calibration flag: `calib.skip_extra_scalings_for_inference=true` for profiles we trust. that prevents adding per-head multiply nodes that block fusion. we'll need evals to check quality impact.

Marco: if we implement the above we should run a focused AB test: 1) current hetero profile, 2) kernel-selector heuristic, 3) smaller batches on fp8 nodes. gather p50/p95/p99 + kv_eviction rate + token-cost.

Priya: i'll open a small PR with: (a) kernel-selector change, (b) new telemetry fields, (c) an infra flag to force smaller batches for seq>2048 on eligible pools. will link the perf traces.

Sara: tagging: @eng-runtime we should consider a short-term opt-in canary for Dedicated customers using qwen-32b to avoid regressions in production. :eyes: 

Pat: one more thought — check our kernel library fallback ordering for older GPUs. fallback to fp8->int8 sometimes picks a suboptimal int8 kernel path. might need a kernel-score recalculation after profiling windows.

Priya: acknowledged. i'll include a microbenchmark matrix (gpu arch x kernel variant x seq x batch) in the PR so we have numeric scores to auto-rank kernels. thanks all. :thumbsup:
